title: When the Sigil Falls Revisited
premise: Astrid Kavanagh makes her living cutting memories from the wealthy and selling them to the desperate, until a mute child arrives at her door speaking Thornfell's dead tongue — the language of the sigil that binds the mountain kingdom together. The child is a living fragment of that sigil, and King Aldric has been hollowed out by the Vessel, an ancient hunger wearing his crown and slowly unbinding the wards that keep the Thornfell passes sealed. Hunted by the king's memory-eaten inquisitors, Astrid and the child, Wren, follow the smugglers' roads to the sigil's buried heart, where Astrid learns she is the last heir of the sigil-smiths who forged it. To rebind the king and seal the passes, Astrid must surrender every memory she has ever stolen — including her own name — but Wren, grown into her own voice, offers to carry the burden instead, splitting it between them so neither is erased.
about_author: Ulyana Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a border-town records office before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about inheritance, found family, and the things we choose to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She lifts a memory from a dying merchant in the city of Greyhollow, showing her trade: extracting recollections with a bone stylus and selling them in vials. The beat is loneliness beneath competence — she keeps one stolen memory of a mother she never had, replayed nightly.

chapters.title: Knocking at the Wrong Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A mud-caked child appears at her attic door during a storm, speaking a language no one alive should know, clutching a shard of black glass that hums. Astrid, against every instinct, lets her in. Beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open a closed life.

chapters.title: Words Older than Walls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. The child remembers being part of something vast — a lattice of light under the mountains — before waking small and alone. Beat: disorientation and grief for a self she can't name.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Smile
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Inquisitor Serane Voss arrives asking about a runaway 'asset,' her eyes glassy with consumed memories. Astrid lies well, but realizes the crown knows the child exists. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Spine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Fleeing Greyhollow through the Thornfell passes only she knows, Astrid tests Wren's strange gift: the child can read echoes of memory left in stone. Beat: wary partnership forming on dangerous roads.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They shelter with Ferro, an old smuggler who owed Astrid's unknown mother a debt — the first hint of Astrid's parentage. Beat: warmth and unease; kindness always costs.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a wayshrine, Wren touches a carved sigil and floods both of them with vision: a king kneeling as smiths forge a binding crown. Beat: awe and terror; the past is not finished with them.

chapters.title: Crown of Hollow Men
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In the capital of Vaelmoor, we see the monarch from inside — a flickering consciousness trapped while the Vessel wears his body, devouring memories to unbind the wards. Beat: horror and pity; the enemy's throne is a prison.

chapters.title: Serane's Hunger
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The inquisitor tracks them, flashbacks revealing she sold her own childhood to the crown for power. Beat: chilling sympathy — she is what Astrid could become.

chapters.title: The Market of Second Lives
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In free-town Brackwater they seek a translator of dead tongues; instead they find a memory-broker who recognizes Astrid's technique — and her face. Beat: identity shaken; someone knew her mother.

chapters.title: Heir of the Sigil-Smiths
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The broker, Ysolde, reveals the Kavanagh line were sigil-smiths, keepers of the binding, thought extinct after the Purge. Astrid refuses the legacy. Beat: anger and denial — inheritance as a chain.

chapters.title: Wren Sings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered by crown soldiers, Wren speaks her first common words — a command that unmakes the soldiers' recent memories. Beat: triumph shadowed by fear of her own power.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro buys their escape with his own memories, handed willingly to Serane as distraction. Beat: sacrifice and heartbreak; belonging means someone pays for you.

chapters.title: Ash Over Vaelmoor
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Vessel burns a ward-village to feed on its collective memory; Aldric surfaces just long enough to leave a plea in his own hand. Beat: dread escalating; the clock is real.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Lining
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Hidden in her mother's old coat, Astrid finds a letter naming the sigil's heart beneath Mount Cael and warning: 'the crown must be unbound by blood that remembers.' Beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Serane Closes In
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. She corners them at a river crossing; Astrid steals three of Serane's memories mid-fight and sees the lonely child she was. Beat: moral complication — enemies are made, not born.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Road
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They descend into the smugglers' deep tunnels, where Wren's presence makes dormant sigils glow, lighting their way. Beat: wonder; the mountain is waking to its heir.

chapters.title: Ghosts Who Kept the Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Echoes of dead sigil-smiths test Wren, mistaking her for their lost fragment. Astrid claims her: 'She's mine, not yours.' Beat: chosen family declared aloud.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ysolde reappears offering a map to the heart in exchange for Astrid's most precious stolen memory — the false mother. Astrid pays. Beat: grief as tuition; letting go to move forward.

chapters.title: The Court of Eaten Things
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Vessel convenes its hollowed courtiers; Aldric's hidden letter reaches a sympathetic maid. Beat: resistance kindling inside the palace.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the ruined smith-archive under Cael's roots, Astrid reads her mother's work-journals and finally mourns her. Beat: acceptance of inheritance as gift, not sentence.

chapters.title: Wren Chooses a Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Asked her true name, Wren refuses the sigil's designation and keeps the name Astrid gave her. Beat: identity as self-authorship; the theme lands.

chapters.title: The Vessel Speaks
chapters.summary: Villain interlude, the Vessel's POV. It was once the first smith's apprentice, betrayed and bound into the crown; it wants release, not conquest. Beat: the antagonist becomes tragic.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ysolde sells their location to Serane to buy back her own consumed daughter's memory. Beat: bitter understanding — everyone bargains with what they love.

chapters.title: Iron and Ash
chapters.summary: Action climax of act two. Serane captures Wren; Astrid escapes wounded into the deep dark alone. Beat: despair, rock bottom.

chapters.title: The Dark Between Sigils
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Lost and bleeding, Astrid hears the mountain itself — her ancestors' voices — and chooses to answer rather than silence them. Beat: rebirth through surrender.

chapters.title: Serane Unbound
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Guarding Wren, Serane touches the child's memory-gift and is flooded with her own sold childhood; she breaks, turns her blade toward Vaelmoor. Beat: redemption earned through pain.

chapters.title: Storming the Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Serane opens the palace gates; Aldric wrestles his body back for ninety seconds to tell them where the crown's keystone hides. Beat: desperate alliance, high velocity.

chapters.title: The Keystone Vault
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They reach the vault beneath the throne; the Vessel springs its trap — it needs a smith's blood to finish unbinding, and Astrid walked into the lock. Beat: trap sprung, stakes absolute.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Stole
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. To activate the rebinding, every stolen memory must be returned or given. Astrid begins pouring hers into the sigil — faces, roads, the false mother — becoming translucent. Beat: devastating cost made visible.

chapters.title: Wren's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Watching Astrid dissolve into the lattice, Wren steps into the circuit and splits the burden, taking half the memories into herself. Beat: love answering sacrifice; the theme of belonging fulfilled.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Climax. Together they pull the Vessel from Aldric's crown; the Vessel, offered its own name and memory by Wren, releases its grip and dissolves weeping into the mountain. Beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Freed and broken, Aldric abdicates rather than rule what he doesn't remember breaking. Beat: accountability; quiet dignity.

chapters.title: The Forgetting Sick
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid wakes with vast gaps — she doesn't know Wren's face, only that she'd die for her. Beat: bittersweet; the cost holds even in triumph.

chapters.title: Relearning Her Own Hands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns Astrid's memories one vial at a time, choosing which to give first. Beat: intimacy rebuilt deliberately; tenderness as labor.

chapters.title: The Smiths' New Charter
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid reforges the sigil order — not hereditary rulers but elected keepers, ending the Purge's old cruelty. Beat: inheritance transformed into stewardship.

chapters.title: Serane's Sentence
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Serane requests memory-work as penance, serving the new charter rather than dying or fleeing. Beat: justice without erasure.

chapters.title: What the Child Carried Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren visits the mountain's heart and leaves the last of the Vessel's grief there, closing the wound for good. Beat: closure; the land exhales.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. One year later, Astrid runs a school for memory-keepers in Greyhollow; another strange child knocks in a storm. She opens the door without hesitation. Beat: full-circle grace.

chapters.title: The Name We Keep
chapters.summary: Dual POV coda. Astrid and Wren climb Cael at dawn; Astrid gives Wren her mother's ring, and Wren gives Astrid back one memory she'd withheld — the night they met, kept safe. Beat: belonging chosen daily; the story closes on warmth.
